texts.preamble: Yathiraj N vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Kabc020115642023 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.2548/2023 Dated this 7th day of August, 2025 Petitioner: Yathiraj S/o Narayanappa, Aged about 36 years, R/at Sidheswaranadurga, Chitradurga, Karnataka - 577 538. (Smt. Raveena K., Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Future Gen. India Ins. Co. Ltd., No.18/1, 3rd Floor, Ashoka Pillar Road, 1st Block, Jayanagara, Bengaluru - 82. 2 Mvc No.2548/2023 (Policy No.V9969110) (Sri Gururaj Salur, Advocate) 2. Thippeswamy S/o Mukundappa, Parashurampura, Challakere, Chitradurga, Karnataka-577 502. Yathiraj N vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125572366/ 1 (Sri B. Pramod, Advocate) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 08-01-2023 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner being a pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-53-W- 2610, was proceeding on Parashurampura-Dharmapura road, near Parashurampura Forest, Chitradurga, the same was ridden by the rider very carefully and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations. At that time, all of a sudden one passenger auto bearing No.KA-16-D-4293, driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, with high speed, came from Doddachelluru road and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Parashurampura and Chitradurga Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident he was Shepherd and earning a sum of Rs.5,00,000/- per annum. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Parashurampura Police have registered the case against the driver of the said passenger auto for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. 4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and its validity as on the date of accident. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. In order to prove his case, the petitioner has got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 16 documents as Ex.P.1 to 16.
texts.arguments: It has contended that, the vehicle in question i.e. auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 is not at all involved in the alleged accident, the same has been falsely implicated in order to get wrongful gain and to make wrongful loss to respondent No.1. The entire police records are manipulated by showing the registration number of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 and seasoned professional have joined hands with the petitioner and manipulated the charge-sheet. Further it is contended that, the petitioner has suppressed the true facts and colluded with the respondent No.2 and the jurisdictional police and fixed false case against the driver of auto-rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293. As per the police Yathiraj N vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125572366/ 2 records there is delay in lodging complaint, the jurisdictional police have filed a false charge-sheet, by creating a false story and implicated the present vehicle and manipulated records. Further it is contended that, at the time of alleged accident, the petitioner was not wearing safety headgear and it is violation of Motor Vehicles Act. Hence, the claim petition is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed. Further it is contended that, on the date of accident, the driver of auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was not holding valid and effective driving licence. The owner of the vehicle has allowed the said driver to drive the same, knowing fully well that he has no valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle and the said auto-rickshaw was not having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply in the place of accident. Hence, there is a violation of policy conditions as well as provisions of Motor Vehicles Act. It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. Whereas, the respondent No.2 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. He has admitted that, he is the owner of the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293 and he has obtained policy bearing No.V9969110 from respondent No.2 Future Generali India Insurance Co. Ltd., for the period 24-03-2022 to 23-03-2023, covering the risk of unlimited liability to 3rd party risk, injury and death, unlimited liability to 3rd party damage and it also covers one driver and three passengers. The above said policy was in force as on the date of accident i.e. 08-01-2023. Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident the driver/insured (Thippeswamy S/o Mukundappa) of the auto- rickshaw bearing No.KA-16-D-4293 was holding valid driving licence to drive the said vehicle. Further it is contended that, the auto-rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-16-D-4293 was havign permit to ply the said vehicle within 10 km from Parashurampura Hobli, issued by Chitradurga RTO, valid from 05-10-2019 to 04-10-2024. The permit was valid as on the date of accident. Further it is contended that, the fitness certificate of said auto rickshaw was valid from 29-09-2022 to 28-09-2024. Hence, the respondent No.1 is liable to pay any compensation ordered by this Court. For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 17. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others , reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." 18. In Yathiraj N vs Future India Gen Ins Co Ltd on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125572366/ 7 such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income. But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence. He has not produced any document to show that, before the accident he was a shepherd and was earning Rs.5,00,000/- per annum. Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.15,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner as Rs.1,86,000/-. b) As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 37 years is 15. Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,86,000 X 20/100 X 15 = Rs.5,58,000/-. ii) Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc. In order to prove the same, he has produced 53 medical bills, as per Ex.P.9. All the bills have been examined carefully and found that the petitioner has spent total amount of Rs.1,62,753/- towards his medical expenses. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,62,753/- under the head of medical expenses.
